reuse.why: The API reuses getScheduledAmount and approximate amounts reuse getApproxNumberThreshold, but five consumers bypass the complete amount helper and retain local dispatch.

duplication.why: Arithmetic is shared, but five consumer blocks still duplicate missing, numeric, ranged, or operator dispatch already handled by the shared helpers.

placement.why: Amount policy belongs in shared/schedules and API projection belongs in api-models, although consumers retain policy dispatch that belongs in the shared definition.

scope.why: The changes are focused on schedule amount policy, its consumers, API exposure, tests, and release notes.

maintainability.why: Shared arithmetic improves ownership, but overlapping exported helpers, repeated caller dispatch, and a loosely typed operator parameter make future policy changes unnecessarily distributed.

bypasses_abstraction.where: createScheduleList, normalizeSchedule, updateActions, postTransactionForSchedule, and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions dispatch locally instead of passing raw amounts and operators to getScheduledAmount.

disguised_duplication.where: The five consumer amount-dispatch blocks replace inline arithmetic with getWorstCaseAmount/getRangedAmount calls while preserving duplicated dispatch already encapsulated by getScheduledAmount.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains the op parameter and delegates to getWorstCaseAmount, which adds an isapprox branch; five consumers bypass the complete helper through local dispatch to lower-level helpers.
